prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "Model" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Benchmark accuracy on he" spans 3 col × 1 row; "Notes" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Model" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 2: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › EN" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 3: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › ZH" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 19px
  col 4: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › AR" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 514px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 446px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 445px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare benchmark accuracy across three model sizes and three language subsets, with notes providing context for each result.","reading":"Readers scan down each language column to compare model sizes, across each row to compare languages, and then consult the notes for context.","groups":["EN, ZH, and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one shared benchmark header; equal widths support comparison.","Model identifies each row, while Notes supplies supporting prose for that row."],"keep_intact":["Model names","Language identifiers EN, ZH, and AR","Individual accuracy values","Words in the benchmark header and notes"],"may_wrap":["The shared benchmark header can wrap between words across the three metric columns.","Notes can wrap naturally; their row heights can also accommodate any wrapping elsewhere in the row."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [60, 55, 55, 55, 220] · table 446×288px · row heights [94, 33, 73, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [65, 70, 70, 70, 170] · table 446×288px · row heights [73, 33, 94, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [60, 45, 45, 45, 250] · table 446×308px · row heights [114, 33, 73, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 1/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
